context: Consider the capacitor in the circuit shown in Fig. 3.10. Let C denote the capacitance in units \unit{F}. The capacitor consists of two parallel plates of area S in \unit{m^2}, separated by a distance d in \unit{m}. The medium between the plates has permittivity \varepsilon; for air, \varepsilon=\varepsilon_0, where \varepsilon_0 is the vacuum permittivity. If the plates are square with side length L in \unit{m}, then S=L^2.

subquestions.subproblem: The capacitor in the circuit in Fig. 3.10
subquestions.solution:
The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is
$$C=\frac{\varepsilon S}{d}$$
For air and square plates with side length L,
$$C=\frac{\varepsilon_0 L^2}{d}$$
subquestions.final_answer_instructions: Your final answer should be given in the form of C = ... . Provide both: (1) the general case written only with \varepsilon, S, d; and (2) the special case for air with square plates written only with \varepsilon_0, L, d.
